items.title: OCR delta sweep (dev/v2.0.0) (PARTIAL) 2026-11-08: 8 findings

labels.name: ocr-sweep
labels.description: Findings from the scheduled Open Code Review (OCR) sweep

items.body:
OCR delta sweep of `dev/v2.0.0` (PARTIAL) found 8 high/critical findings. Full JSON in the run artifact:
https://github.com/cbtw-apac/HarborRAG/actions/runs/42457448133
Some files were not reviewed; the marker was not advanced and they will be retried.

- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/connection_records.py:48-48`
  All operations in this repository accept a bare caller-supplied `tenant_id` and never receive or validate a `StorageOperationContext`. A caller can therefore pass another tenant's ID to read its documents/tasks or purge its records, bypassing the required storage-boundary tenant check. Require the context on these operations and reject a tenant mismatch rather than treating the ID as authorization.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/v1/admin/connection_schemas.py:100-102`
  These request models accept raw connector secrets (including arbitrary string values), and `put_connection`/`test_connection` pass them directly into the credential-writing/testing service. This violates the API security rule that HTTP requests must never supply connector credentials and exposes secret material to API request handling and any request telemetry; remove credential values from both HTTP bodies and provide a separate approved provisioning mechanism.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/workflow_control/control_plane/connections.py:333-337`
  The default `origin="api"` only blocks new `env:` references; raw strings in secret fields still pass through `_plan_credentials` and are persisted by this writer. The HTTP PUT route supplies those values directly, and `test()` likewise resolves raw form values into a connector. This violates the API rule that requests must not supply connector credentials. Reject raw secret values on API-origin writes/tests (or route clients through a non-secret credential mechanism) before storing or resolving them.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-core/src/harborrag_core/domain/connection_snapshot.py:40-40`
  Only `credentials` are checked here. A snapshot can be constructed or restored with sensitive fields in `config` or `tuning`, and `to_json()` persists those values while `secret_refs` only tracks credential references. Validate all three mappings before accepting a snapshot so plaintext secrets cannot enter persisted revisions through these fields.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/connection_records.py:104-109`
  This unconditionally deletes pending/running/paused task rows. The connection-deletion flow checks for an active run before beginning removal, but that check is not synchronized with sync admission/submission; a sync can register its task after the check and continue while this purge removes it. Coordinate deletion with the sync lease or reject/serialize purge while an active task exists so a worker cannot run against a removed task/connection.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/ops.py:48-48`
  `ApiSettings.metrics_scrape_token` accepts an empty `SecretStr`. With that configuration, `token` is `b""` and an `Authorization: Bearer ` header passes this comparison, exposing `/metrics` to any caller on the ops port. Reject empty configured tokens or treat an empty token as unset/unauthorized.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/api/v1/chat/replay.py:43-43`
  Persisted chat idempotency claims keep the request hash across deployments, but the old schema serialized `tenant` and `max_steps` while this schema serializes `tenant_id` and omits `max_steps`. Since existing chat claims are retained, retrying an otherwise identical completed request after upgrade hashes differently and is rejected as a conflict instead of replaying the saved result. Normalize the fingerprint across schema versions (or migrate retained hashes) so the documented safe-retry behavior survives upgrades.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-app/src/harborrag_app/workflow_control/control_plane/connections.py:532-534`
  This active-run check is not coordinated with `sync()`: sync acquires `connection-sync:...`, but delete neither acquires that lease nor atomically marks the connection deleting before checking. A sync can pass its checks, then delete can observe no task, mark deleting and start removal while the sync submits/starts its task. Use a shared per-connection guard or an atomic status transition and recheck submissions so ingestion cannot begin after deletion has committed its state.

items.body:
## Contexto
O entregável 2 da v0.1 é "conecte um projeto GCP **ou importe logs manualmente**". A Importação manual é o caminho mais curto para o piloto avaliar incidentes históricos.

## História de usuário
Como **Analyst**, quero enviar um arquivo de logs exportado, para diagnosticar falhas de sistemas que ainda não têm Conector.

## Escopo
- Bucket privado `raw-logs` no Supabase Storage, com caminho `{tenant_id}/imports/{import_id}/{filename}`. Policy do Storage: escrita e leitura apenas quando `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = app.current_tenant_id()::text`.
- Upload direto do navegador com **URL assinada de upload** emitida pela API (`POST /api/v1/imports` retorna `upload_url` e `import_id`). Upload resumível (TUS) para arquivos acima de 6 MB.
- Limites: 50 MB por arquivo e formatos `.json`, `.ndjson`, `.csv` (checagem por extensão **e** por magic bytes e parse). Outros formatos são recusados.
- Tabela `imports (tenant_id, id, integration_id, filename, size_bytes, sha256, format, status check in ('uploaded','processing','done','failed','rejected'), total_lines, accepted, rejected, duplicates, secrets_removed, error, created_by, created_at)`.
- Tabela `raw_log_objects (tenant_id, id, storage_path, sha256, size_bytes, source check in ('import','connector','api'), expires_at)`.
- Ao concluir o upload (`POST /api/v1/imports/{id}/complete`), grava uma mensagem `ingestion.raw` na outbox. O worker de #12 faz o parse em streaming.
- CSV: tela de mapeamento de colunas para o Contrato de evento, com sugestão automática por nome de coluna e mapeamento salvo por Integração.
- Linhas rejeitadas guardadas com o motivo (`import_rejections`), para download.
- Tela 13: área de upload, progresso em tempo real (Realtime em `imports`) e resultados.

## UI — Tela 13
```text
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ ← Importar logs          │
│ Integração [Pedidos ▾]   │
│ ┌ ⇪ Escolher arquivo ──┐ │
│ │ JSON, NDJSON, CSV 50MB│ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ │
│ sap-order….ndjson [Norm.]│
│ ████████░░ 8.120/12.600  │
│ bapi-errors.csv [Concl.] │
│ 2.004 ev · 14 rej · 3 seg│
└──────────────────────────┘
```

## Critérios de aceite
- **Dado** um arquivo `.xml`, **quando** enviado, **então** a importação fica `rejected` com a mensagem "Formato não permitido".
- **Dado** o mesmo arquivo (mesmo sha256) enviado duas vezes para a mesma Integração, **então** a segunda importação é marcada como duplicada e não gera Eventos novos.
- **Dado** um arquivo de 12 mil linhas, **quando** processado, **então** o progresso atualiza ao menos a cada 2 s na tela.
- **Dado** um usuário do tenant B, **quando** tenta ler o objeto de A no Storage, **então** recebe `403`.

## Segurança / LGPD
- O Log bruto expira conforme a retenção (30 dias padrão, #29) e não aparece em listagens públicas.
- O conteúdo passa pela Sanitização (#13) **antes** de virar Evento.

## Testes
- Fixtures CSV e NDJSON com linhas inválidas, encoding latin-1 e BOM.
- Teste de isolamento das policies do Storage.

## Dependências
#8, #10

---

items.title: Tracker: taxonomy, ontology and knowledge-graph integrity audit (2026-11-14)
items.body:
Mike requested a deeper taxonomy/ontology/knowledge-graph audit and durable GitHub issues before implementation planning.

## Scope and evidence boundary
Audited source: [main 20fda901e3](https://github.com/Mikecranesync/MIRA/tree/20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f), checked 2026-11-14. This is a specialist findings tracker under #5232, not a replacement execution tracker or an implementation claim.

Covered: crawler and Hub entity writers; proposal mapping/deduplication/approval; approval lifecycle; Postgres migrations; graph traversal and context formatting; graph query traces; i3X projection; ontology/SHACL fixtures and CI; graph-context entry points. Public code and synthetic examples only.

Evidence obtained:
- Executed actual pinned Python functions for fault identity and supersession with synthetic collaborators.
- Executed actual pinned TypeScript functions using Node 24 type stripping and injected synthetic DB/traversal collaborators: canonical mappings, proposal dedup query contract, document approval lookup, branch formatting, and i3X type/parent projection.
- Re-ran `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mira-ontology-review-deps python tools/validate_ontology.py`: **28/28 checks pass; fixture-coverage check SKIP; 11/42 shapes have a targeted invalid fixture, 31 uncovered**. Passing fixtures do not establish runtime enforcement.

These are source-level/synthetic reproductions, not live PostgreSQL, deployed app, physical-device, or human-acceptance proof. No production data inspected or changed. No provider/model evaluation, migration, code fix, merge, deployment, or graph approval performed.

## Inventory
The bounded source audit produced **9 defect groups and 2 validation/integration gaps**, each filed separately. Proposed P1/P2 ordering is scoped to this audit, not an override of the canonical pilot tracker.

| Issue | Finding | Evidence | Proposed order |
|---|---|---|---|
| #5520 | Model/fault/manual identities collide under display-name keys | Executed fault-key probe + schema/writer analysis | Foundation |
| #5521 | Re-ingestion changes facts while preserving approval | Explicit upsert-column analysis | Foundation |
| #5522 | Document approval confuses KG UUID and upload UUID | Executed actual helper with distinct synthetic IDs | Foundation |
| #5523 | Supersession leaves approved KG state unchanged; canary conflates states | Executed transition + reader/canary analysis | Foundation |
| #5524 | Dedup suppresses directed/revised proposals | Executed query-contract probe | Foundation |
| #5519 | Canonical approved types/directions disagree with readers | Executed mapping + reader SQL inspection | Foundation |
| #5525 | Branches become false chains; topology conclusions overstate evidence | Executed formatter + algorithm analysis | Context correctness |
| #5527 | Traces use names and lack durable graph/source receipts | Retrieval/trace source analysis | Evidence correctness |
| #5526 | i3X unresolved types and request-dependent parent IDs | Executed projection functions | Interoperability |
| #5528 | 31 shapes lack targeted negative fixtures; runtime mapping unproven | Actual validator run + tree/call-site inspection | Validation gap |
| #5529 | One graph-backed technician journey still needs integrated proof | Entry-point/flag source inspection | Integration gap |

The issues include concrete synthetic cases, source permalinks and acceptance criteria. Implementation tests are still to be committed by their eventual owners. Main was rechecked after filing and remains `20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f`.

Existing issues retained rather than duplicated:
- #3383 — entity-id ON CONFLICT target disagrees with natural-key migrations; additional current callers need coverage.
- #3399 — integration-suite CI coverage needs current reconciliation: current CI does run selected real-Postgres suites; do not repeat the old blanket “none run” claim.
- #5238 — canonical Asset Memory and evidence reuse coordination.
- #3708 — existing asset-creation/graph-bridge follow-up; current completion not established in this audit.
- #3233 — existing asset/telemetry alias identity follow-up; current deployed state not established here.

## Proposed repair plan and dependencies
1. **Reconcile and reproduce:** assigned owner refreshes main/active claims, identifies the correct deployed schema, and commits failing disposable-Postgres tests for the existing #3383 plus new findings. Preserve the original expected answers and existing evidence. Scope changed rows read-only before any repair/backfill.
2. **Identity and approval:** decide scoped identities (#5520) together with #3383, so fixing ON CONFLICT does not introduce silent collisions. Bind approved facts to revisions (#5521); resolve document IDs (#5522), supersession (#5523), and lifecycle-aware directional dedup (#5524). These share writer/approval files and need a coordinated, serialized owner.
3. **Relationship/read contract:** align canonical names AND directions (#5519); prove writer→human approval→reader on the same database. Then preserve branches, uncertainty and limits in context (#5525). A new graph database would not repair these contracts.
4. **Receipts and interoperability:** carry exact graph/source/revision IDs (#5527), then reconcile i3X type and parent references (#5526). Reuse the existing Postgres and source-record/version/evidence capabilities. i3X work can remain outside the immediate pilot unless required by its chosen journey.
5. **Validation and product proof:** add the relevant ontology fixtures/mappings (#5528) alongside each repair; then integrate and measure one technician workflow (#5529), with #5238 as the existing Asset Memory lane. Require exact-revision CI, deployed citation checks and separate human acceptance before capability closure.

Expand only after measured benefit and unchanged wrong-model, stale-evidence, tenant-isolation, and abstention protections.

No graph-database replacement, broad rewrite, or “GraphRAG prevents hallucinations” acceptance claim. Current pilot/manual repairs retain their existing owners and priorities. A green unit test, merged PR, and technician acceptance are separate states.

## Remaining audit/closure work
- [ ] Refresh main and active PR/owner claims before implementation; compare any changed files with this pinned audit.
- [ ] Identify the correct authorized MIRA database/environment and read-only reconcile applied schema and aggregate affected-row counts; do not query unrelated projects.
- [ ] Run migrations plus writers/approval/readers against disposable PostgreSQL with synthetic tenants.
- [ ] Verify deployment flags and route reachability; source existence is not evidence that a path is enabled.
- [ ] Reproduce and then close affected workflows on the actual deployed app, including citations and graph evidence.
- [ ] Obtain technician acceptance for the selected bounded workflow without rewriting expected answers to match output.

“Inventory complete” means this bounded audit is reconciled; it does not mean every possible defect in MIRA has been discovered.

## Existing work and overlap
Open PR titles were reviewed (first 100 most recently updated); selected file lists checked. This is not an exhaustive ownership clearance:
- #5504 already changes the Notebook chat route and adds bench-component identity/selection. #5529 must coordinate there instead of opening a competing chat rewrite.
- #4091 owns upload/ingest/source lifecycle files and also Notebook/node chat; #5520/#5522 must reconcile upload identity with that work.
- #5042 changes equipment-notebooks source supersession for #4083. It does not edit the KG node-document-proposals upsert audited here; reuse its source/version semantics while retaining the separate KG identity finding.
- #5241 / #5238 owns Asset Memory/evidence integration and Notebook chat. The first 100 files include those shared seams; no claim that its full file list was audited.
- Existing #5510/#5517 and other applicability/variant repairs remain with current owners. New KG issues do not establish that those repairs are obsolete or replace their acceptance.
- #3383 received current-caller evidence; #3399 received the current-CI correction. No existing issue was closed, reassigned or rewritten.

items.title: Mock audit returns "Not recorded" when product lookup fails (follow-up to #3609)
items.body:
Non-blocking follow-up from review of #3609 (https://github.com/regengine/RegEngine/pull/3609), raised in Grok's review: https://github.com/regengine/RegEngine/pull/3609#pullrequestreview-5648754106

**Current behavior** — https://github.com/regengine/RegEngine/blob/main/services/ingestion/app/mock_audit.py#L311

```python
scenario["target_product"] = _get_product_for_tlc(tenant_id, real_tlc) or "Not recorded"
```

`_get_product_for_tlc` (mock_audit.py:54) returns `None` when the lookup fails or finds no row. Since `product_description` is NOT NULL in `alembic/sql/V002__fsma_cte_persistence.sql`, `None` should only happen on a lookup failure, yet it is shown as "Not recorded". That label tells the user the product was never recorded and hides the real failure.

**Suggestion**
- Distinguish a lookup error from a genuine missing value: log the failure and surface an explicit lookup-error / empty state (e.g. a `target_product_error` flag or a non-200 response) instead of the "Not recorded" literal.
- Add a test that forces the lookup to fail and asserts the error state is surfaced.

Not a blocker for #3609, which is merged.

items.title: 8th step
items.body:
```python
import base64
import json
import logging
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, Response, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from agent_orchestrator import VideoAgentOrchestrator

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger("videomesh-worker")

app = FastAPI(
    title="VideoMesh Agent Orchestrator Worker",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="Cloud Run Pub/Sub push subscriber for agentic video deconstruction",
)

# --- Pydantic Schemas for Pub/Sub Push Payloads ---

class PubSubMessage(BaseModel):
    data: str = Field(..., description="Base64-encoded string payload from Pub/Sub")
    attributes: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    message_id: Optional[str] = None
    messageId: Optional[str] = None
    publish_time: Optional[str] = None
    publishTime: Optional[str] = None


class PubSubPushEnvelope(BaseModel):
    message: PubSubMessage
    subscription: str


class IngestionJobPayload(BaseModel):
    jobId: str
    tenantId: str
    youtubeUrl: str
    timestamp: Optional[str] = None


# --- Background Worker Runner ---

def run_agent_pipeline(job_id: str, youtube_url: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
    """Executes the end-to-end agentic ingestion pipeline in a background thread."""
    logger.info(f"Starting execution for Job ID: {job_id} (Tenant: {tenant_id})")
    try:
        orchestrator = VideoAgentOrchestrator(
            job_id=job_id,
            youtube_url=youtube_url,
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
        )
        orchestrator.execute()
        logger.info(f"Successfully finished execution for Job ID: {job_id}")
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error(f"Fatal error during execution of Job ID {job_id}: {exc}", exc_info=True)


# --- HTTP Endpoints ---

@app.get("/healthz", status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
async def health_check() -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Liveness/readiness probe for Cloud Run."""
    return {"status": "healthy", "service": "videomesh-worker"}


@app.post("/", status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)
async def handle_pubsub_push(
    envelope: PubSubPushEnvelope,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
    request: Request,
) -> Response:
    """Receives and acknowledges Google Cloud Pub/Sub push subscription messages."""
    if not envelope.message.data:
        logger.warning("Received Pub/Sub push with empty message data. Acknowledging to avoid redelivery.")
        return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)

    # 1. Base64 Decode and Deserialize Payload
    try:
        decoded_bytes = base64.b64decode(envelope.message.data)
        decoded_str = decoded_bytes.decode("utf-8")
        payload_dict = json.loads(decoded_str)
        job_data = IngestionJobPayload.model_validate(payload_dict)
    except Exception as err:
        logger.error(f"Failed to parse Pub/Sub push message: {err}. Raw data: {envelope.message.data}")
        # Return 200 to drop poison pills into Dead-Letter Queue rather than infinite retries
        return Response(
            content=json.dumps({"error": "Malformed payload dropped"}),
            media_type="application/json",
            status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
        )

    logger.info(f"Received verified job push: {job_data.jobId} for URL: {job_data.youtubeUrl}")

    # 2. Hand Off to Background Worker
    # Acknowledge HTTP 200 immediately to Pub/Sub to prevent timeout-induced redelivery loops.
    background_tasks.add_task(
        run_agent_pipeline,
        job_id=job_data.jobId,
        youtube_url=job_data.youtubeUrl,
        tenant_id=job_data.tenantId,
    )

    return Response(
        content=json.dumps({"status": "ACCEPTED", "jobId": job_data.jobId}),
        media_type="application/json",
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    )

```

---

### Critical Cloud Run & Pub/Sub Provisioning Commands

Because `background_tasks.add_task` executes after the HTTP response has been delivered, Cloud Run must be provisioned with **CPU always allocated** (`--no-cpu-throttling`) to prevent the container's CPU from idling while downloading video streams or running Gemini inference.

```bash
export PROJECT_ID="videomesh-production"
export REGION="us-central1"
export SERVICE_NAME="videomesh-worker"
export TOPIC_NAME="video-ingestion-jobs"
export SUB_NAME="video-ingestion-push-sub"
export SA_NAME="pubsub-cloudrun-invoker"

# 1. Create a Dedicated Service Account for Pub/Sub Push Invocations
gcloud iam service-accounts create $SA_NAME \
    --display-name="PubSub Cloud Run Invoker"

# 2. Deploy Worker with No CPU Throttling and 15-minute Timeout
gcloud run deploy $SERVICE_NAME \
    --image="gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/videomesh-worker:latest" \
    --platform=managed \
    --region=$REGION \
    --memory=4Gi \
    --cpu=2 \
`````

items.title: Core: authoritative tenant-scoped ITSM ↔ Incident/Run cross-reference
items.body:
## Problem

The current GLPI→Copilot fast path can extract a unique `RUN-...` reference from a ticket title/description and verify that the Run exists in Core. That proves only the existence of the referenced Run, not that the GLPI ticket is authoritatively linked to it or belongs to the same tenant. A text reference can be copied, forged or stale. The Portal/AI must not promote that to `LINKED`.

## Target architecture

Core remains the sole owner of the canonical cross-system relationship. GLPI remains authoritative for the ticket itself; Core stores a verified, tenant-scoped association and its provenance. Portal/NOC/Copilot consume the same read contract.

## Required contract

- Authenticated, tenant-scoped Core write path for recording a GLPI ticket association, callable only by a trusted integration adapter or approved workflow.
- Immutable/audited association event with tenant, source system, GLPI instance identity, ticket ID, canonical incident/run ID, source event/reference, actor/service identity, verification method, observed/known timestamps, mapping version and idempotency key.
- Read API returns `VERIFIED`, `UNKNOWN`, `CONFLICT`, `STALE` or `UNAUTHORIZED`; no title/description heuristic can produce VERIFIED.
- Enforce same-tenant ownership for ticket, incident, run and CI before exposing any link or Copilot context.
- Reconciliation must detect missing, duplicate, superseded and conflicting links without guessing.
- Keep GLPI writes out of scope; initial vertical slice is authenticated read-back and synthetic adapter contract only.

## Acceptance tests

1. Unique RUN ID in ticket text with no Core mapping remains UNKNOWN.
2. Copied/forged RUN ID cannot link a ticket to a different incident.
3. Cross-tenant ticket/run association is denied before returning context.
4. Conflicting or stale mapping returns CONFLICT/STALE, never LINKED.
5. Verified mapping is idempotent and append-only; superseding mappings preserve history.
6. Copilot receives a run binding only after the Core API returns VERIFIED for the authenticated tenant.
7. 401/403/UNAVAILABLE remain distinct and fail closed.

## 48h delivery

First inspect the current Core schema and existing cross-reference tables; reuse existing data structures if safe. Implement the smallest main-based change with migration only if required, unit/contract tests and ephemeral DB integration. Do not copy the stacked PR #192/#193 implementation wholesale.

## Safety

Read-only GLPI. No LIVE approval, remediation, SSH/sudo, direct DB bypass, deployment or production migration. Missing identity/mapping/tenant evidence is UNKNOWN.

items.title: W5-06 · Threat-intel data model: a record that isn't a `Finding`

milestone.title: Week 5 — Analytics and Threat Intelligence
milestone.description: Independent, self-paced continuation. No assignees or fixed deadline. Plan: https://github.com/emad-anwer/buguard-internship-planning/blob/main/docs/weeks/week-05.md

items.body:
> **Self-paced continuation:** The internship has ended. Complete this work independently in your own checkout. Week numbers are learning stages, not deadlines. No assigned owner, reviewer, or mentor approval is required.

**Effort:** 3h · **Depends on:** W5-01

🔑 the threat-intel track's foundation. W5-07, W5-08, W5-09 and W5-10 are all behind it.

## What

The first real code in `src/app/modules/intel/` — `models.py`, `repository.py`, `service.py`,
`route.py`, `schemas.py`, `api.py`, six empty files since week 1, same as every module package was
before its week arrived.

Implement the data model ADR-0005 decided. Concretely, whatever the ADR says, this is very likely a
`Vulnerability` (or similarly named) table keyed on CVE ID, **not** inheriting `TenantOwnedMixin` and
**not** a `Finding`/`FindingKind` — a CVE is true for every tenant and owned by none, and the roadmap
defers matching it against a tenant's assets to week 7. If the design review decided otherwise, implement
that instead, but the repository layer should make the decision impossible to get wrong by accident:
don't reach for `TenantScopedRepository` out of habit if this table has no `tenant_id` to scope by.

Shape, following ADR-0005's join-key decision: one row per CVE, with columns (or a related table, if
that's what was decided) for whatever CISA KEV, NVD and EPSS each contribute — KEV's
"known exploited since" date, NVD's description/CVSS/CPE references, EPSS's score and percentile —
and an explicit representation of "this source hasn't reported on this CVE yet" that isn't just a
column silently left at its SQLAlchemy default.

A plain repository (not `TenantScopedRepository`) with the basic operations the next four tasks
need: upsert-by-CVE-ID (idempotent — three different ingestion jobs will all call this), read by ID,
and a filtered list (by KEV status, by minimum EPSS score, by minimum CVSS) for W5-10's read API.

Tests:

- A CVE upserted twice with the same ID updates the existing row rather than creating a duplicate
- A CVE with only KEV data populated, then later updated with NVD data, then later with EPSS data,
  ends up as one row with all three, not three rows or three tables disagreeing
- The model has no `tenant_id` column (or, if your ADR justifies otherwise, a test and the ADR both say
  why)
- A query by CVE ID that doesn't exist returns `None`/empty, not an exception

## Expected outcome

`src/app/modules/intel/` has a working model, repository, and the empty `service.py`/`route.py`
scaffolding ready for the next four tasks to fill — and a reviewer can look at `models.py` and
immediately see it's a different shape from `core/models.py`'s `Finding`, not a copy of it with the
tenant column removed as an afterthought.

## Think about

This is the first table in the codebase with no `tenant_id`, and the instinct to add one "to be
safe" is exactly the thing ADR-0005 should have argued against. A `tenant_id` on a global vulnerability
catalog doesn't make it safer — it makes every row either duplicated per tenant for no reason, or
nullable in a way that means nothing. If you find yourself wanting one, that's a sign the model is
drifting back toward `Finding`, and it's worth re-reading what the design review actually decided before
writing the column.

The idempotent upsert matters more than it looks like it should: three separate ingestion jobs
(W5-07, W5-08, W5-09), on three separate schedules, all touch the same row for the same CVE. If two
of them run close together and the upsert isn't safe under that, the record for a real CVE ends up
depending on which job happened to run last — silently.

## Search for

- sqlalchemy upsert on conflict do update
- cve id format and canonical representation
- database schema for records with partial data from multiple sources
- repository pattern without tenant scoping

## Planning source

[Task brief](https://github.com/emad-anwer/buguard-internship-planning/blob/main/tasks/week-05/W5-06-threat-intel-data-model.md) · [Stage plan](https://github.com/emad-anwer/buguard-internship-planning/blob/main/docs/weeks/week-05.md)

**Prerequisite issues:** [W5-01](https://github.com/emad-anwer/tem-platform/issues/123)

items.title: DFC: define CI-run ingestion contract for Propel/FFT events
items.body:
**Prerequisite** extracted from lornu-ai/propel#11 (API-first integration). Filed because #11's FFT change can't be built until DFC accepts CI-run events.

## Gap
#11 wants FFT/Propel to emit CI-run events to DFC instead of writing SurrealDB directly, but DFC's current contract rejects them:
- Routes are `POST /v1/events/aivcs` and `POST /v1/events/hitl` (`crates/dfc-server/src/main.rs:111-112`) — there is no generic `/ingest`.
- Event-type allowlist is `aivcs.*` / `hitl.*` only (`crates/dfc-core/src/ingest.rs:6-17`); `propel.run.*` / `fft.ci.*` are rejected.
- `source_system` enum is `{aivcs_api, aivcs_human_in_the_loop, data_fabric}` (`schemas/dfc-event.schema.json`) — no propel/fft.
- `dfc.v1` schema is `additionalProperties:false` and requires `tenant_id` + `idempotency_key`; a `{checks,status,duration_ms,sha}` body is rejected.

## Ask (pick one)
- **A:** Add a first-class CI ingestion path: `source_system: propel`/`fft`, event types `propel.run.completed` / `fft.ci.completed`, and the CI fields in `dfc.v1` (or a `payload_ref`), on `POST /v1/events/ci` (or extend an existing route).
- **B:** Document the adapter mapping from CI runs onto the existing `dfc.v1` envelope so producers can conform (tenant_id, idempotency_key, event_id `^evt_`, allowed source_system) — no schema change.

## Acceptance
- A Propel/FFT CI-run event is accepted (2xx), normalized to `dfc.v1`, and forwarded to data-fabric.
- Contract (host `dfc.aivcs.io`, route, schema) is documented for producers.

Blocks: lornu-ai/propel#11 (FFT half).

items.title: P0: Establish canonical Cataran platform contracts and ownership before three-plane release
items.body:
## Why this is a release blocker

The current audit cannot find the planned `ugai-platform-contracts` or `ugai-platform-admin` repositories through the installed GitHub search. UGAI, IM19 and Notebook already carry overlapping task, identity, approval, event and artifact contracts. A 404/search miss is not proof a private/alternate repository does not exist, and this issue does not authorize creating a new repository.

## Required Master Architect decision

1. Identify and accept one canonical home for versioned platform contracts (existing repo, new repo, or a controlled transitional directory).
2. Assign a contract owner and change-control process. Runtime repositories consume versioned contracts; they must not independently redefine them.
3. Publish schema packages/specifications for:
   - Identity / Principal / Tenant / Membership / Project
   - Task / TaskState / TaskEvent / Idempotency
   - Approval / ApprovalReceipt / SideEffectPolicy
   - MCP connection / tool invocation / audit
   - A2A dispatch / callback
   - Evidence / provenance / artifact
   - Audit / outbox / replication / error envelope
4. Define stable identifiers, issuer/subject semantics, tenant scoping, actor semantics, timestamps, digest formats, version compatibility and deprecation policy.
5. Build language-appropriate generated/client types and contract test fixtures.
6. Publish a consumer matrix showing UGAI, IM19, Notebook, Cloudbrowser, RAG_Cerdas and Android Connector versions.
7. Add schema compatibility CI and a migration/rollback plan before changing runtime contracts.

## Initial observed conflicts

- Notebook API membership uses (tenant_id, subject, status), while Supabase Auth membership uses (tenant_id, user_id UUID) with a distinct role vocabulary.
- UGAI PR #23 carries a durable task/approval contract and IM19 client adapter.
- IM19 PR #33 has its own gateway/connector DTOs.
- Cloudbrowser task dispatch and callback need to use the same task/event identities.
- RAG_Cerdas provenance and artifact references need a stable evidence contract.

## Acceptance gates

- One reviewed schema source and a consumer compatibility matrix.
- Golden fixtures validated by every active repo's CI.
- Breaking contract changes fail CI until an explicit version bump and migration path exists.
- No duplicate MCP gateway responsibility.
- Architecture Owner review and exact-SHA CI results before production use.

## Scope / safety

No repository is created or renamed by this issue. Do not merge or deploy cross-repo runtime changes until the canonical contract location and ownership decision is recorded.

items.title: Change request: Define usage event contract v1 and idempotent per-kind usage ingestion
items.body:
kind: feature
Risk: R2

## Change request

- Request: `3d275314-1b5d-5052-ab74-7e999bcba54b` revision 1
- Project: `falcone-serverless`
- Target repository: `gntik-ai/falcone`
- Proposal fingerprint: `sha256:9035d6e55758680ddd2efa18cb3647a27b980e4794f1fb2ace3175df09fd1972`

## Backlog decomposition

- Story: gntik-ai/falcone-serverless#37 (TEN-02)
- Epic: gntik-ai/falcone-serverless#8
- Task: `TEN-02.t4`
- Plan: `55292b52-afd6-49fd-b31f-1c9d204220b7` (sha256 `382ab4d0efba874ff93bf14c39c39aa1746d867ab190447aef2262f25b0315c1`)
- Predecessor tasks: `TEN-01.t2`
- Depends on: gntik-ai/falcone#1337

<!-- hermes-decomposition plan=55292b52-afd6-49fd-b31f-1c9d204220b7 task=falcone-serverless:TEN-02.t4 -->

## Why

- TEN-02 acceptance requires failed attempts, retries, cold starts and warm idle capacity to generate distinct usage records. FR-TEN-03 also lists builds, storage, WebSocket connections and messages, and interactive and batch execution among the dimensions whose charging Falcone owns. The frame makes TEN-02 the early provider of ctr-usage-events v1; OBS-03 and OCI-08 extend it. The contract carries facts only, never prices. Execution usage belongs to a workspace, while warm idle capacity belongs to a tenant/profile pool. Storage follows the per-kind usage constraints of the TEN-01.t2 scope registry, and ingestion is tested against that migrated schema so both kinds can actually be stored.

## What changes

- Publish ctr-usage-events v1 under docs/contracts/serverless/usage-events/. It defines idempotent usage units keyed by stable attempt and event IDs; the record kinds attempt, failed attempt, retry attempt, cold start, warm idle capacity, build, storage, WebSocket connection and WebSocket message; the workload class (interactive or batch); and the runtime mode.
- Map each record kind to a TEN-01.t2 usage scope_kind. Execution-derived kinds are stored as execution usage with verified tenant and workspace IDs. Warm idle capacity on a tenant/profile pool is stored as tenant pool usage with tenant_id, the pool ID and no workspace_id.
- Implement the contract in a Falcone ingestion path that deduplicates by event ID and stores records into the migrated usage table under the matching scope_kind.
- Add reconciliation of usage totals against attempt records, and ship conformance fixtures for every kind.
- Add adapter tests that apply the TEN-01.t2 migration and ingest every kind, including warm idle capacity, into the real table.

## Out of scope

- Charging configuration (TEN-02.t5).
- Producing records from dispatch (TEN-02.t6) and from pool observations (TEN-02.t7, TEN-02.t8).
- OCI pod-seconds, idle warm time and image storage kinds (OCI-08); metering pipelines and dashboards (OBS-03).

## Affected repositories

- `gntik-ai/falcone` (source)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] docs/contracts/serverless/usage-events/ defines v1 with distinct kinds for failed attempts, retries, cold starts, warm idle capacity, builds, storage, and WebSocket connections and messages, and its fixtures pass pnpm run test:contracts.
- [ ] Ingesting a fixture of a failed attempt, its retry with a cold start and a warm idle interval stores distinct records of each kind, and delivering the same events twice counts each once.
- [ ] Adapter tests against the migrated schema store a warm idle record as tenant pool usage with no workspace_id, and execution-derived records with tenant and workspace IDs. A warm idle event carrying a workspace ID, or an execution event without one, is rejected and not stored.
- [ ] A contract test rejects any price or charging field.
- [ ] Usage totals reconcile with attempt records in a test, and pnpm run test:unit, pnpm run test:adapters and pnpm run lint pass.

## Risks

- Kinds fixed now constrain OBS-03 and OCI-08; they may only add kinds additively.
- A record kind mapped to the wrong scope_kind would fail at the database; the adapter tests cover every kind.

Proposed risk R2: Usage records do not change the sandbox, host capabilities, egress, secrets or tenant isolation; the story risk note is R2.

## Rollout

- Record usage before enabling charging; charging is enabled per plan after reconciliation passes.

## Kill switch

- Disable ingestion by configuration; attempt records stay authoritative for a later backfill.

## Open questions

- DEP-01, STO-01 and INV-03 produce the build, storage and WebSocket usage facts. This task defines their kinds so those producers can emit them, and validates the kinds with fixtures until the producers exist.

## Independent review

- Reviewer: codex
- Decision: APPROVE after 1 round(s)
- Summary: The proposal matches the task scope and supplied requirements. It distinguishes future implementation from current code, defines independently testable acceptance criteria compatible with the listed commands, preserves tenant-pool versus workspace execution scope, and reasonably assigns R2 risk. Producer integration and charging remain outside this task.
- Unresolved findings: none

## Operator description

> Backlog decomposition 55292b52-afd6-49fd-b31f-1c9d204220b7, task falcone-serverless:TEN-02.t4 of story TEN-02 (gntik-ai/falcone-serverless#37).
> Target: gntik-ai/falcone (source), component quotas; size M, about 8 files.
> Covers: TEN-02#ac3; requirements: FR-TEN-03.
> Interfaces provided: ctr-usage-events; consumed: ctr-usage-events.
> Paths: docs/contracts/serverless/usage-events/; apps/control-plane/.
> Test commands: pnpm run test:unit; pnpm run test:contracts; pnpm run test:adapters; pnpm run lint.
> Predecessor tasks: falcone-serverless:TEN-01.t2.
> Sources: design §2 FR-TEN-03; design §4 TEN-02; TEN-02#ac3; frame ctr-usage-events; frame global decision on shared record scope; frame global decision on workspace-scoped execution data.
