items.title: Module #37: Statutory Clock & Immutable Discovery Timestamp (reasonable_grounds_at)
items.body:
### Architectural Requirement (POPIA s22(1))

#### Problem
In POPIA compliance, the statutory clock ("as soon as reasonably possible") begins at the moment there are **reasonable grounds to believe** that personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person — not at the conclusion of internal digital forensics or executive triage.

#### Implementation Requirements
1. **Immutable Discovery Timestamp**: Implement `reasonable_grounds_at` as a strictly immutable, timezone-aware UTC datetime.
2. **Audit Logging**: Any alert ingestion or anomaly detection crossing the "reasonable grounds" heuristic threshold must emit an append-only audit record establishing statutory trigger time.
3. **Clock Monitoring**: Expose calculated elapsed time against configured tenant SLA limits (alerting before common regulatory delay thresholds).

Ref: Module #37 Architecture Specification.

items.title: [FEAT] Enterprise Security: OAuth2/OIDC Authentication (Keycloak/IdP) and Granular Multi-Tenant Job RBAC/ABAC

labels.name: java
labels.description: Pull requests that update java code

items.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

OpenCrawling champions **Zero-Trust RAG and Data Ingestion**, enforcing strict access control lists (ACLs) and enterprise permission preservation across vector stores, repositories, and search outputs. However, the orchestration plane itself—specifically the **REST APIs**, the **Admin UI (`oc-admin-ui`)**, and the **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server**—currently operates without a centralized authentication and authorization layer.

For an enterprise platform, unauthenticated management endpoints represent a non-negotiable security, compliance, and governance violation:
> **If the downstream RAG is Zero-Trust, the upstream orchestration that configures pipelines, triggers ingestion, and manages data stores must be Zero-Trust as well.**

Currently:
1. **Lack of Authentication**: Any client with network access can invoke the REST API to trigger, pause, stop, create, or delete crawling jobs, alter pipeline configurations, or view sensitive execution traces.
2. **No Multi-Tenant / Departmental Segregation**: In large enterprise deployments, different departments manage disparate ingestion pipelines (e.g., the HR team configures pipelines to extract employee records from Alfresco, while Finance manages accounts payable contracts on OnBase/SharePoint). Currently, any user in the Admin UI can see and control every job. An HR administrator must not be able to start, stop, modify, or inspect the logs of Finance jobs.
3. **Missing Auditability & Data Lineage**: When a job fails, stalls, or overwrites critical target datasets (such as Apache Ozone claim-check buckets or PostgreSQL pgvector collections), the platform cannot definitively prove which user or authorized AI agent triggered that specific execution.
4. **Unsecured MCP Tool Access**: Corporate LLMs interfacing with OpenCrawling's built-in MCP server currently interact with tools without inheriting the caller's enterprise identity, risking unauthorized cross-departmental job inspection or execution.

---

## Describe the solution you'd like

We propose implementing an enterprise-grade security architecture based on **OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (OIDC)** and **Granular Role-Based & Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/ABAC)** across the OpenCrawling ecosystem:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Identity_Provider ["Identity Provider (Keycloak / Entra ID / Okta)"]
        IDP["OIDC / OAuth2 Provider\n(MFA, SSO, LDAP/AD Federation)"]
    end

    subgraph Clients ["Clients & Interfaces"]
        UI["Admin UI (oc-admin-ui)\n[OIDC PKCE Flow]"]
        CLI["OpenCrawling CLI (oc-cli)\n[Bearer Token / Device Flow]"]
        SDK["Java Client SDK (oc-java-client-sdk)\n[OAuth2 Client Credentials]"]
        LLM["Enterprise LLM Agent\n[MCP with User Security Context]"]
    end

    subgraph Orchestration ["Orchestration Tier (oc-runtime)"]
        GATEWAY["Spring Security FilterChain\n(JWT Bearer Token Validation & JWKS)"]
        RBAC["JobPermissionEvaluator\n(RBAC/ABAC Enforcement)"]
        CONTROLLER["JobController / SystemController\n(@PreAuthorize)"]
        AUDIT["JobLedgerAccumulator & Audit Lineage\n(Principal Stamping)"]
    end

    subgraph Storage ["Persistence Tier (PostgreSQL)"]
        JOB_DB[("jobs Table\nowner, tenant_id, allowed_groups")]
        AUDIT_DB[("Parquet Job Reports & Logs\ntriggered_by, caller_roles")]
    end

    IDP -.->|Issues Tokens| UI
    IDP -.->|Issues Tokens| CLI
    IDP -.->|Issues Tokens| SDK
    IDP -.->|Issues Tokens| LLM

    UI -->|JWT Bearer Token| GATEWAY
    CLI -->|JWT Bearer Token| GATEWAY
    SDK -->|JWT Bearer Token| GATEWAY
    LLM -->|JWT / Delegation Context| GATEWAY

    GATEWAY --> RBAC
    RBAC -->|Authorize Action| CONTROLLER
    CONTROLLER --> AUDIT
    AUDIT --> JOB_DB
    AUDIT --> AUDIT_DB
```

### 1. Delegated Identity Management via OAuth2 & OIDC (Keycloak & Enterprise IdPs)
Leveraging Spring Boot's native OAuth2 Resource Server and OIDC capabilities (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server`):
* **Zero Credential Storage in OpenCrawling**: Completely delegate identity lifecycle, password hashing, and user credential storage to enterprise-grade Identity Providers (Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory, Okta, Ping Identity).
* **Enterprise Features Out of the Box**: Natively inherit Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), session management, and LDAP/AD synchronization without custom authentication code in OpenCrawling.
* **Stateless JWT Verification**: The backend validates standard RSA/EC signed JWT bearer tokens against the IdP's JWKS endpoint (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`), caching public keys locally.

### 2. Granular Multi-Tenant Access Control on Jobs (RBAC / ABAC)
Transform OpenCrawling from a single-tenant system tool into a secure multi-tenant platform:
* **Departmental & Tenant Segregation**: Model jobs with ownership and access control metadata (`owner`, `tenant_id`, `allowed_roles`, `allowed_groups`).
* **Declarative Spring Security Enforcement**: Protect management endpoints using method security:
  ```java
  @PreAuthorize("hasPermission(#jobId, 'Job', 'EXECUTE')")
  @PostMapping("/{id}/start")
  public ResponseEntity<JobResponse> startJob(@PathVariable("id") String jobId) { ... }

  @PreAuthorize("hasPermission(#jobId, 'Job', 'READ')")
  @GetMapping("/{id}")
  public ResponseEntity<JobDTO> getJobById(@PathVariable("id") String jobId) { ... }
  ```
* **Custom `PermissionEvaluator`**: Compare the caller's JWT claims (`preferred_username`, `groups`, `realm_access.roles`) against the job's ACL to permit or deny `READ`, `WRITE`, `EXECUTE`, or `ADMIN` actions.
* **Filtered Job Listing**: When listing jobs (`GET /api/jobs`), automatically filter results to return only the jobs the authenticated caller has permission to view.

### 3. Comprehensive Audit Lineage & Data Provenance
* Capture the authenticated caller's identity (username or AI Agent service account) in every execution context (`MDC`, OpenTelemetry trace attributes).
* Stamp the triggering principal (`triggered_by: "john.doe@company.com"`, `roles: ["hr-admin"]`) into:
  * Runtime job state transitions.
  * Ingestion event envelopes (`JobExecutionCompletedEvent`).
  * Parquet and Avro historical execution ledgers generated by `JobReportService` / `ParquetJobReportGenerator`.

### 4. Admin UI (React / Vite) OIDC Integration
* Integrate standard Authorization Code Flow with PKCE in `oc-admin-ui` (via `oidc-client-ts` or `@react-keycloak/web`).
* Intercept Axios requests in `src/lib/api.ts` to automatically attach the active `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, with automatic token refresh on expiration.
* Provide user profile and role indication in the Admin UI header, rendering job controls (Start, Stop, Delete, Edit) conditionally based on user permissions.

### 5. Security Context Propagation for the MCP Server
* Corporate LLMs invoking OpenCrawling's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server endpoints will inherit and propagate the user's security context.
* MCP tools (`fetchJobTraces`, `listAccessibleSources`, `secureVectorSearch`, and job management tools) evaluate caller permissions, ensuring an LLM agent acting on behalf of an HR user cannot access or trigger Finance ingestion pipelines.

---

## Detailed Technical Specification & Implementation Plan

### 1. Core Models & Persistence (`oc-core` & `oc-runtime`)
- [ ] Add `JobSecurityConfig` domain model in `oc-core`:
  * `owner: String` (User ID / email of creator)
  * `tenantId: String` (Optional multi-tenancy partition key)
  * `allowedGroups: List<String>` (e.g. `["hr-team", "crawling-operators"]`)
  * `allowedUsers: List<String>`
- [ ] Update `JobDTO` and PostgreSQL schema for `jobs` table:
  * Add columns: `owner VARCHAR(255)`, `tenant_id VARCHAR(100)`, `allowed_groups JSONB/TEXT`, `allowed_users JSONB/TEXT`.
  * Support migration of existing legacy jobs with default administrator ownership.
- [ ] Implement `JobPermissionEvaluator` implementing Spring Security's `PermissionEvaluator`:
  * Evaluate permissions: `READ`, `WRITE`, `EXECUTE`, `DELETE`, `ADMIN`.
  * Superadmin bypass for global platform administrators (e.g. `ROLE_OPENCRAWLING_ADMIN`).

### 2. Spring Security & OAuth2 Resource Server Configuration (`oc-runtime`)
- [ ] Add `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server` dependency in `oc-runtime/pom.xml`.
- [ ] Create `SecurityConfig.java`:
  * Configure `SecurityFilterChain` with JWT resource server decoding (`jwk-set-uri` or `issuer-uri`).
  * Implement `KeycloakJwtAuthenticationConverter` to map Keycloak realm/client roles and custom group claims into Spring Security `GrantedAuthority` collections.
  * Permit unauthenticated access to Swagger/OpenAPI docs and health checks (`/actuator/health`).
  * Require authentication for `/api/**` and MCP endpoints.
- [ ] Add configuration properties under `spring.opencrawling.security`:
  * `enabled`: boolean (default `true` in production profiles; `false` in dev profile for optional local development without IdP).
  * `issuer-uri` / `jwk-set-uri`: OIDC provider metadata endpoint.
  * `client-id`: Expected audience/client identifier.
  * `admin-role`: Name of role granting superadmin capabilities (default: `opencrawling-admin`).

### 3. Audit Logging & Lineage (`oc-runtime`)
- [ ] Update `JobOrchestrator.java` to extract `Authentication` from `SecurityContextHolder`.
- [ ] Inject `triggeredBy` into `JobReportSummary` and `JobLedgerAccumulator`.
- [ ] Include caller identity in Parquet job reports generated for Apache Ozone / S3 data lakes.

### 4. Admin UI Authentication (`oc-admin-ui`)
- [ ] Add OIDC client library (e.g. `oidc-client-ts`).
- [ ] Support environment configuration: `VITE_OIDC_AUTHORITY`, `VITE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_OIDC_SCOPE`.
- [ ] Add Axios request interceptor in `src/lib/api.ts` to attach `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- [ ] Add authentication state provider, Login/Logout flow, and user profile badge in navigation bar.
- [ ] Conditionally disable/hide job actions based on the user's groups.

### 5. Client SDK & CLI (`oc-java-client-sdk` & `oc-cli`)
- [ ] Update `DefaultJobClient` in `oc-java-client-sdk` to support static Bearer token or OAuth2 client credentials token provider.
- [ ] Add authentication options in `oc-cli` (`--token`, `--client-id`, `--client-secret`, `--token-url` or `oc auth login`).

### 6. Containerized Reference Architecture & Documentation
- [ ] Add `docker/docker-compose-with-keycloak.yml` containing:
  * Keycloak 26 container with pre-configured `opencrawling` realm.
  * Pre-configured clients (`opencrawling-admin-ui`, `opencrawling-api`).
  * Sample demo users: `hr_admin` (roles: `hr-team`), `finance_admin` (roles: `finance-team`), `global_admin` (roles: `opencrawling-admin`).
- [ ] Add enterprise documentation: `docs/Security-and-Identity-Management.md` with setup guides for Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and Okta.

---

## Additional Context & References

* **Zero-Trust Strategy**: Extends OpenCrawling's downstream Zero-Trust ACL model to the orchestration and administration plane.
* **Open Ingestion Standard (OIS)**: Aligns with OIS permission and identity models.
* **Spring Boot Reference**: [Spring Security OAuth2 Resource Server](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/resource-server/index.html)
* **Keycloak Documentation**: [Securing Applications and Services Guide](https://www.keycloak.org/documentation)

items.title: Implement bulletproof ingestion roadmap and automatic tenant provisioning
items.body:
## Objective

Execute the remaining bulletproof-ingestion roadmap, beginning with the confirmed fresh-account tenant-provisioning defect.

**Implementation reference:** `PLAN-bulletproof-ingestion.md` is the normative reference for this issue and every implementation subtask. Where the plan describes an older repository shape, preserve the requirement while using the current architecture documented below.

## Confirmed auth root cause

Fresh registration and OAuth account creation write the account to MongoDB, and authentication can create a Redis session/JWT, without creating the authoritative PostgreSQL personal tenant and membership.

Current sequence:

```text
register / first OAuth login
  -> Mongo account exists
login / OAuth callback
  -> credentials accepted; session/token can be issued
first tenant-gated HTTP/WebSocket/document request
  -> PostgreSQL app_tenant_memberships lookup finds no row
  -> request fails as "No tenant membership found" (normally surfaced as 403)
```

The defect is therefore usually **post-login authorization failure presented as login failure**, not bad credentials.

Evidence:

- `src/app/features/auth/service.py::AuthService.register` calls `account_store.create()` and returns success without provisioning SQL.
- The OAuth new-account path similarly creates an account/session without SQL tenant provisioning.
- `src/app/features/auth/dependencies.py::get_current_authorization_context` correctly treats PostgreSQL membership as authoritative and fails closed.
- `src/app/features/auth/tenant_migration.py` creates deterministic personal tenants/memberships for legacy Mongo accounts.
- The **full** migration provisions missing SQL state:
  `uv run python scripts/migrate_personal_tenants.py`
- `--reconcile` does **not** create a missing tenant or membership. It only repairs the Mongo mirror for an existing SQL membership marked pending:
  `uv run python scripts/migrate_personal_tenants.py --reconcile`

This explains why running the full migration repairs an affected user and why reconcile-only is not a registration solution.

## Approved auth design

Use **synchronous authoritative provisioning backed by a durable saga/outbox**.

### Invariant

> Registration/account creation is not complete, and no login/refresh/OAuth session may be issued, until the authoritative SQL personal tenant and membership exist.

Create one deep auth-owned interface used by every account-creation path, for example:

```python
PersonalTenantProvisioner.provision(
    user_id: UserId,
    display_name: str,
    legal_roles: tuple[LegalRole, ...],
) -> ProvisioningResult
```

Its implementation owns SQL transactions, idempotency, lifecycle state, mirror synchronization, durable repair, and observability.

### Required flow

1. Create the Mongo account with explicit provisioning state `pending`.
2. In one PostgreSQL transaction:
   - upsert `app_tenants(id="personal:<user_id>")`;
   - upsert the corresponding `app_tenant_memberships` row;
   - write initial legal roles and role revision;
   - stage a durable provisioning/outbox record.
3. Commit PostgreSQL.
4. Best-effort update the Mongo tenant mirror using revision-monotonic compare-and-set.
5. Return completed registration / issue a session only after SQL membership existence is confirmed.
6. If mirror synchronization fails, keep SQL authoritative, mark reconciliation pending, and repair asynchronously.
7. If SQL provisioning fails, keep the account pending and issue no normal session.

Use database-native `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`; do not implement concurrency safety as read-then-insert.

Invoke the same provisioner from password registration, OAuth first-account creation, administrative creation/imports, invitations, and future SCIM flows. Login and refresh perform an invariant check before session issuance; they are not the primary provisioning mechanism.

### Error semantics

| Condition | Required result |
|---|---|
| Invalid credentials | Existing typed authentication failure |
| Correct credentials, durable provisioning pending | Typed `ACCOUNT_PROVISIONING_PENDING`, retryable; never report invalid credentials |
| SQL unavailable while provisioning/checking | Retryable infrastructure error, normally 503; never map to 403 |
| Mongo account creation failure | Registration fails; no completed SQL/account state claimed |
| SQL tenant/membership failure | Account remains pending; no session |
| SQL commit succeeds, Mongo mirror fails | Account is usable through SQL authority; reconciliation pending |
| Duplicate/concurrent provisioning | Deterministically returns the same tenant/membership |
| Old mirror update arrives after a newer revision | Reject with revision-monotonic compare-and-set |

A product-facing pending response may be `202 provisioning_pending` during registration and `409 ACCOUNT_PROVISIONING_PENDING` during login; use `503` when provisioning state cannot be checked because SQL is unavailable.

---

## Current plan audit

Audit basis: current tree at `94d40cb004a701d549d2f9557af1b4e74ffd48d8`, the on-disk plan, and the live code paths. Counts use independently actionable plan units rather than stale task checkboxes.

### Totals

| Classification | Count |
|---|---:|
| Implemented | 6 |
| Partially implemented | 15 |
| Not implemented | 9 |
| Superseded by a better design | 1 |
| Intentionally deferred | 2 |
| **Total audited plan units** | **33** |

The auth provisioning defect is an additional prerequisite and is not counted as one of the 33 original plan units.

### Implemented — 6

| # | Plan unit | Current evidence | Why this classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | C1 multi-contract fixture | `evals/golden/legal_retrieval_v2.jsonl`, manifest and multi-contract boundaries | The corpus includes explicit multi-contract cases and expected `contract_index` labels. |
| I2 | C2 scanned/OCR fixtures | `evals/corpus/`, v2 manifest OCR metadata and OCR semantic-flip cases | Scanned/no-text-layer and OCR-risk artifacts exist with provenance. |
| I3 | C3 bounded upload guardrails | `src/app/shared/upload_validation.py`; both document and compatibility routers | Extension/MIME/empty checks and bounded `max_size + 1` reads prevent unbounded buffering. |
| I4 | C4 document/model-call budgets | LangExtract extraction configuration and persisted Agent Saul budget ledger | Contract count, passes/calls, time, token/cost and concurrency boundaries are enforced. |
| I5 | C5 multi-contract classification boundary | `src/app/features/documents/classification.py`; `service/ingest.py` | Conservative boundary detection and per-contract extraction are live. |
| I6 | C6 `contract_index` end to end | chunk model/migrations, Graphiti identity, evidence handles, findings/citations and retrieval graph state | Contract identity survives ingestion, storage, graph write/read, retrieval and reporting. |

### Partially implemented — 15

| # | Plan unit | Implemented portion | Missing portion / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | C7 source/OCR fidelity | OCR-enabled parsing, typed warnings, `completed_with_warnings`, OCR metadata in evals | Production ingestion does not persist authoritative source coverage, ordering, OCR confidence/coverage, table/section-loss or chunk-plausibility metrics. |
| P2 | C8 untrusted-document injection safety | Evaluation schema/cases classify prompt injection, fake system/tool output and urgent directives | No queued-ingestion fixture proves embedded instructions cannot affect parties, boundaries, tenant scope, metadata or graph group identity. |
| P3 | C9 truthful lifecycle/terminal events | Idempotent attempts, terminal outbox, retry-exhaustion bridge, dead-letter path and monotonic fencing | No stuck-age detector/alert and UI notification behavior has not been proven end to end. |
| P4 | C9 cache/idempotency scope | Tenant, allowed docs, evidence policy, document/pipeline versions and session identity are widely bound | Re-ingestion replacement/retention semantics and every stale-version transition are not yet proven as one lifecycle. |
| P5 | C10 ingestion gold set | v2 corpus contains about 105 labeled, provenance-audited legal retrieval cases | CI validates schema/provenance; it does not run representative files through the queued source-to-chunk pipeline and gate fidelity. |
| P6 | Phase D graph relationship path | Typed relationship schemas and an idempotent Graphiti writer exist | Production ingestion still supplies an empty relationship list; the second grounded extraction pass is absent. |
| P7 | Re-ingestion prerequisites | `pipeline_version`, version-aware retrieval/cache identities and evidence metadata exist | Graph replacement/supersession, old-version retention and stable historical EvidenceRef policy are incomplete. |
| P8 | Phase F legal agent tools | Read-only evidence and graph-facing tools are wired under server authorization | Relationship-dependent tools operate over a graph with no production relationship edges, limiting truth and usefulness. |
| P9 | G1 eval corpus depth | Corpus grew far beyond the original four cases and has strong provenance/adjudication structure | It is below the plan's 150–300 target and lacks a weekly feedback-fed growth loop. |
| P10 | G1 retrieval metrics | Experiment harness and deterministic graders exist | Recall@k, MRR and nDCG are not yet the routine queued-ingestion/retrieval CI decision gate across query classes. |
| P11 | G2 contextual retrieval | Docling hybrid chunker extracts deterministic heading/context preambles; search and reranking consume them | This is metadata contextualization, not the plan's measured 1–2 sentence document-aware context summary. |
| P12 | G4 Graphiti as retrieval signal | Graphiti narrowing/filtering and contract-scoped groups exist | Relationship traversal is not a measured fourth fused branch because production edges do not exist. |
| P13 | G6 observability | Structured logs, OpenTelemetry foundations, budget controls and worker timing exist | There is no single per-stage trace for plan→embed→branches→fusion→rerank→grade→generate. |
| P14 | G6 economics/escape metrics | Some token, model-call, latency and cost budgets are recorded | Answer-cache hit rate, grade-loop escape rate and cost per answered query are not first-class product metrics. |
| P15 | North-star observability | Typed readiness/degradation states and evidence policy/coverage are exposed | Fidelity loss is still not consistently materialized on the document record; some truths remain only in logs/eval metadata. |

### Not implemented — 9

| # | Plan unit | Evidence / gap | Why it remains |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | Phase B explicit relationship-skipped truth state | `service/ingest.py` still aggregates `clause_results` and empty `relationship_results` with `all(...)` | `all([]) is True` still collapses “not attempted” into success. |
| N2 | Phase D grounded second-pass relationship extraction | TODO remains in the LangExtract-to-graph path; ingestion passes `[]` | The writer was built before a producer; security/fidelity work was prioritized. |
| N3 | Phase E quarantine ledger | `docs/quarantine-ledger.md` is absent | Retained dormant surfaces lack explicit port/discard criteria and revisit triggers. |
| N4 | Phase F/G3 retrieval unification | `/search/ask` and `/legal/ask` still use inline `ask`; compiled retrieval graph remains unmounted | Switching without parity evidence would be a risky behavior change. |
| N5 | G5 small-to-big retrieval | No clause-hit → structural-parent hydration path | Existing grouping is token-bounded adjacency, not parent-section retrieval. |
| N6 | G7 feedback loop | No thumbs/citation-click/reviewer-correction promotion pipeline | There is no production usage-to-eval compounding loop. |
| N7 | G8 late-chunking experiment | No measured late-chunking comparison | Correctly withheld until evaluation depth is sufficient. |
| N8 | G8 multi-query expansion experiment | No measured expansion comparison | Correctly withheld until evaluation depth and stage economics exist. |
| N9 | G8 semantic-cache experiment | No measured near-duplicate semantic cache comparison | Correctly withheld until correctness/isolation behavior can be evaluated. |

### Superseded by a better design — 1

| # | Original plan | Current design | Why better |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Phase A unmount `/ingestion/documents/upload` and return 404 | The endpoint remains deprecated but delegates to the canonical tenant-aware documents ingestion service, with deprecation metadata/telemetry | One canonical implementation preserves client compatibility and avoids a second write truth; remove/410 it only after telemetry confirms no callers. |

### Intentionally deferred — 2

| # | Plan unit | Deferral condition |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Re-ingestion as product/admin/agent capability | Keep unexposed until replacement/version/supersession, old-version retention and historical evidence identity are fully specified; then expose only as an audited, approval-gated operator action. |
| D2 | Agentic multi-hop retrieval and additional model-mediated stages | Do not add until deterministic retrieval, fidelity gates, eval depth, per-stage cost and parity evidence demonstrate a measurable need. |

### Top gaps

1. Fresh accounts can authenticate before authoritative tenant provisioning.
2. Empty relationship extraction is reported through success-shaped aggregation.
3. Ingestion fidelity is not mechanically measured and persisted.
4. Injection resistance is represented in eval labels but not proven through the real queued ingestion path.
5. CI does not exercise the real queued source→chunk→index pipeline.
6. The knowledge graph has clause episodes but no grounded legal relationship edges.
7. Inline and compiled retrieval implementations can drift.
8. Contextual/small-to-big retrieval benefits are unmeasured.

---

## Ordered implementation phases

Implement in exactly this order. Each phase ends with its own green validation boundary and conventional commit.

### 1. Automatic account/tenant provisioning

Implement the approved hybrid synchronous provisioner + durable saga/outbox described above.

Acceptance:

- Password registration and OAuth first-account creation produce authoritative SQL tenant/membership before success/session.
- All account-creation paths use one provisioner.
- Login, refresh and WebSocket admission enforce `session issued => SQL membership exists`.
- Concurrent calls create exactly one deterministic tenant/membership.
- SQL success + Mongo mirror failure remains usable and reconciles.
- SQL failure creates no normal session and returns typed pending/infrastructure semantics.
- Migration remains the legacy repair mechanism, not a normal registration dependency.
- Fix any authorization error mapping that turns retryable SQL failure into 403/500.

### 2. Explicit relationship-skipped truth state

Remove vacuous success semantics.

Acceptance:

- Clause success is evaluated independently.
- If relationship extraction did not run, emit/persist a typed `graph_relationships_skipped` result with reason `relationship_extraction_not_implemented`.
- “Not attempted,” “succeeded with zero edges,” and “failed” are distinct.
- Add regression coverage preventing `all([])` from reappearing as success.

### 3. Fidelity + ingestion prompt-injection gates

Materialize fidelity on the document/attempt record:

- source text/page coverage;
- source-order preservation;
- OCR coverage/confidence or explicit unavailability;
- table/section preservation;
- implausible chunk-count and empty-output detection;
- typed degraded/warning/failure thresholds.

Run untrusted-document fixtures through the actual queued ingestion path. Prove embedded instructions cannot change authorization, `tenant_id`, `allowed_doc_ids`, contract boundaries, authoritative metadata, Graphiti group IDs, or extraction policy.

Acceptance:

- Every uploaded document completes, completes with typed warnings, or fails with a specific reason.
- Fidelity metrics and their provenance survive into status/reporting.
- No model-derived value can widen authorization or overwrite server-owned identity.
- Thresholds are configurable, versioned and observable.

### 4. Queued-ingestion CI benchmark

Turn representative v2 corpus artifacts into a deterministic source→parse→chunk→extract→persist benchmark.

Acceptance:

- CI runs representative clean, scan/OCR, table, annexure, irregular numbering, multi-contract, injection, near-miss and failure cases.
- Reports source coverage, ordering, OCR/table/section fidelity, chunk plausibility, multi-contract identity and terminal-state truth.
- CI first reports a baseline; enforcement thresholds are enabled only after variance is understood.
- Normal CI is frozen/offline and checksum-verified.
- A corrupted checksum and an untruthful success fixture demonstrably fail validation.

### 5. Grounded relationship extraction

Add the plan's second, semantically different LangExtract pass.

Acceptance:

- Pass 2 consumes pass-1 entity identities/attributes and emits typed relationships.
- `from_node`/`to_node` must resolve to pass-1 identities; never create endpoints from fresh free text.
- Every edge contains a canonical `clause_id`, citation/page/span, document version and `contract_index`.
- Writes use the existing idempotent Graphiti writer.
- Re-ingestion creates no duplicate active edge.
- Contract fixtures yield expected obligations/overrides/definitions/party relations.
- The Phase-2 skip state disappears only for document classes that actually ran relationship extraction.

### 6. Retrieval unification only after parity evaluation

Compare inline `ask` against the compiled graph before routing traffic.

Parity dimensions:

- tenant/document/version/contract scope;
- evidence policy and citation support;
- retrieval recall/precision/nDCG;
- answer correctness/coverage/abstention;
- cache/idempotency behavior;
- failure/degradation semantics;
- latency and cost.

Acceptance:

- Fixed-set parity report is checked in.
- No scope/security regression.
- Route `/search/ask` and `/legal/ask` through one deep retrieval module only after thresholds pass.
- Remove the duplicate only after its replacement is live and proven.

### 7. Contextual + small-to-big retrieval only if measured benefit

Run controlled experiments, do not assume benefit.

Variants:

- current deterministic heading preamble;
- document-aware 1–2 sentence contextual preamble;
- clause-level retrieval with structural parent-section hydration.

Acceptance:

- Evaluate by query class, especially definitions, cross-references, provisos, schedules and amendments.
- Adopt only if supported-claim quality/recall improves without unacceptable precision, latency or cost regression.
- Context generation is amortized/cached and versioned.
- Parent hydration is token bounded and preserves exact evidence citations.
- Kill/revert criteria are documented before experiments run.

---

## Migration and rollout

- Add a durable provisioning lifecycle marker/backfill compatible with existing accounts.
- Keep the existing full migration as idempotent legacy repair.
- Keep `--reconcile` strictly mirror repair; rename/help text/docs must make that distinction unambiguous.
- Add a readiness gate proving every active account has exactly one valid personal membership unless deliberately team-only.
- Run full migration, reconciliation, then `--check` before rollout.
- Deploy provisioning behind an observable feature flag if needed, but never mint sessions for unprovisioned accounts.
- Add counters for pending age, provisioning failures, mirror failures/retries and invariant-blocked login/refresh.
- Alert on any active account missing authoritative membership and any provisioning item exceeding the SLO.
- Preserve SQL as authorization authority; Mongo is an identity/audit mirror.
- Rollback must not delete tenant ownership or memberships.

## Security requirements

- Server-generated tenant/user/document/contract/version identity only.
- Never derive authority from document text, model output, checkpoint state or Mongo mirror.
- Fail closed on missing/ambiguous membership; distinguish outage from denial.
- Revision-fence Mongo mirror updates.
- Bind all evidence, Graphiti, cache and idempotency operations to tenant + allowed docs + document/pipeline version + contract identity.
- Treat all uploaded content as untrusted.
- No model-callable provisioning, re-ingestion or mutating graph tool.
- Audit account provisioning, authorization denial, evidence access, relationship writes and reviewer actions.
- Preserve raw source/evidence outside graph checkpoints.

## Observability

Required traces/metrics:

- account provisioning: Mongo create, SQL transaction, outbox stage, mirror sync, reconciliation and time-to-ready;
- ingestion: upload validation, parse/OCR, boundary classification, chunking, extraction pass 1/2, persistence, Graphiti writes and terminal event;
- retrieval: plan, embedding, lexical/vector/graph branches, fusion, rerank, grade, generate;
- answer-cache hit rate;
- grade-loop escape rate;
- cost and latency per completed/degraded/failed document and per answered query;
- stuck document/provisioning age;
- `graph_relationships_skipped/succeeded/failed` counts.

Do not log confidential source text or secrets.

## Test requirements

At minimum:

1. Password registration → verification → login → tenant-scoped upload without migration command.
2. OAuth first account → session → tenant-scoped request.
3. SQL provisioning failure → pending/no session.
4. SQL commit + mirror failure → usable via SQL and eventually reconciled.
5. Concurrent provisioning → exactly one tenant/membership/outbox intent.
6. Crash after SQL commit → durable repair convergence.
7. `--reconcile` alone does not claim to provision missing SQL.
8. Full migration repairs legacy missing SQL state.
9. Login/refresh/WebSocket reject truly unprovisioned accounts with correct typed semantics.
10. Stale mirror revisions cannot overwrite current authorization.
11. Relationship skipped/success/failed states are distinct.
12. Fidelity threshold tests for OCR, ordering, tables, sections, empty output and chunk plausibility.
13. Injection fixtures cannot alter server-owned identity/policy.
14. Queued benchmark covers clean, messy, multi-contract and failure inputs.
15. Relationship endpoints/citations resolve to pass-1 canonical identities.
16. Relationship re-run idempotency.
17. Inline-vs-compiled retrieval parity before cutover.
18. Contextual/small-to-big experiments include predeclared kill thresholds.
19. Cross-tenant, cross-document, stale-version and wrong-contract negative tests.
20. Existing provenance, Ruff, Ty, compile, Alembic, evaluation and full test gates remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not make `--reconcile` an account-provisioning mechanism.
- Do not provision tenants lazily in generic authorization dependencies.
- Do not weaken SQL-authoritative authorization to preserve login UX.
- Do not expose re-ingestion yet.
- Do not make provisioning, re-ingestion or graph mutations model-callable.
- Do not add agentic multi-hop retrieval before parity/eval/economics justify it.
- Do not add late chunking, multi-query expansion or semantic caching in these seven phases.
- Do not replace pgvector/cross-encoder infrastructure without measured evidence.
- Do not silently delete quarantined surfaces; document explicit port/discard criteria.
- Do not treat model-generated summaries, OCR or extracted relationships as authoritative evidence without canonical spans.

## PR and merge gate

Implementation may use multiple conventional commits but lands through one reviewable PR tied to this issue.

Before merge:

- all acceptance criteria for the included phases are checked with command evidence;
- migrations and rollback/irreversibility are reviewed;
- CodeRabbit reports no blocking findings;
- Greptile reports **5/5 merge confidence**;
- all P0/P1 review findings are fixed or explicitly rejected with evidence;
- full relevant test/type/lint/eval/provenance gates pass;
- no scope/security regression;
- final PR description lists deferred work and measured experiment outcomes.

**Do not merge without Greptile 5/5 and a clear CodeRabbit review.**

## Completion definition

This issue is complete when:

- new users can register/login/use tenant-gated features without a migration command;
- the ingestion pipeline never represents skipped work as success;
- fidelity degradation and injection resistance are mechanically tested through the real queue;
- grounded legal relationships exist with canonical citations;
- one retrieval implementation survives after measured parity;
- contextual/small-to-big retrieval is adopted only if it wins the predeclared evaluation;
- required review gates approve the PR.

> The important invariant is not “the happy path usually creates enough records.” It is that no externally visible success can exist without its authoritative fact: no session without membership, no graph success without attempted writes, no supported claim without canonical evidence, and no architecture upgrade without measured benefit.

items.title: Hackathon [Feature]: Microsoft Entra ID Data-Source Connector
items.body:
### Problem Statement

cognee has no Microsoft-identity connector. Tenants run on Entra ID (users, groups, app registrations, sign-in/audit logs) and that knowledge ("who is Guest vs Member, which service principals own which apps, what sign-ins failed?") never reaches memory.

### Proposed Solution

Add an `entra` connector in cognee-community, following the shape of the existing connectors, over Microsoft Graph v1.0.

- **Auth**: OAuth2 client credentials (`ENTRA_TENANT_ID`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_ID`, `ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET`), scopes `User.Read.All`, `Group.Read.All`, `Application.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`. No review for own tenant.
- **Ingest**: users (UPN, displayName, accountEnabled, userType), groups + transitive members, applications/service principals, sign-in logs + audit logs. One document per user (groups + apps folded); logs folded per user-day.
- **Selection**: `include_users/groups/apps/logs`, `user_type=["Member"]`, `sign_in_days=30`.
- **Incremental sync**: `$filter=... gt {cursor}` + `$orderby` + `@odata.nextLink` paging; **delta queries** (`/users/delta`, `/groups/delta` with `$deltatoken`) for true deltas including tombstones. Per-doc hash skips unchanged.
- **Forget-on-delete**: delta tombstones (`@removed`) map to deletes; full-snapshot fallback purges orphans. Empty-page-with-state aborts.
- **Privacy**: UPNs columns-only with hash in prose; client secrets/keys never fetched.

```
packages/connector/entra/
├── README.md
├── cognee_community_connector_entra/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── entra.py
│   └── auth.py
├── examples/
│   └── basic_usage.py
├── tests/
└── pyproject.toml
```

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Use Case

1. **Guest audit** — ask "which Guests still have access to Finance group?"
2. **App ownership** — sync service principals; ask "who owns the payroll app registration?"
3. **Sign-in triage** — ask "which accounts failed MFA this week?"


### Implementation Ideas

_No response_

### Additional Context

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A user connects via tenant credentials and selects what to ingest
- [ ] Selected content is ingested and searchable in cognee

items.title: Idempotency for usage ingestion to prevent duplicate billing
items.body:
# Idempotency for usage ingestion to prevent duplicate billing

## Summary
Duplicate usage events can lead to over-billing or noisy compensating logic. Add first-class idempotency to the ingestion path so producers can safely retry without creating duplicate charges. Context: real-time metering at scale often involves retries and at-least-once delivery.

## Problem
- Clients and network retries can send the same usage event multiple times.
- Kafka at-least-once delivery can surface duplicates to consumers.
- Without dedupe, duplicates inflate usage and require manual corrections.

## Proposed solution
- API: Accept `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID v4) and/or `event_id` in the body. If missing, compute a deterministic hash from `tenant_id + metric + timestamp bucket + value`.
- Storage: Add unique index on `(tenant_id, idempotency_key)` in the durable usage store (e.g., `usage_events`). On conflict, return `200` with `idempotent: true`.
- Kafka path: Support consumer-side dedupe with a small TTL’d table keyed by `(tenant_id, idempotency_key)`, or optionally a compacted topic keyed by `idempotency_key`.
- Responses:
  - First write: `200 { success: true, idempotent: false, idempotencyKey }`
  - Duplicate: `200 { success: true, idempotent: true, idempotencyKey }`
- SDKs: Provide helpers to set `Idempotency-Key` and persist across retries.
- Observability: Emit metrics for idempotent hits; log at debug.

## Data model
- Table: `usage_events`
- Columns: add `idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL`
- Unique index: `(tenant_id, idempotency_key)`
- Migration: backfill as nullable -> set default/generated when omitted -> migrate to `NOT NULL`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Posting the same event concurrently multiple times results in a single stored record.
- API returns `idempotent: true` on duplicates.
- Consumer path drops duplicates when replayed.
- Benchmarks show minimal overhead at target QPS.

## Alternatives considered
- Time-window dedupe only (inexact for long retry windows).
- Consumer-only dedupe (duplicates still hit storage/aggregation layers).

## Risks
- Potential index hot-spotting; mitigated with `(tenant_id, key)` and UUID keys.
- Slight write amplification; acceptable for correctness.

items.title: ai(smriti-byoa/AI-07/AI-11/INT-13): External Agent Memory Gateway — Zero-Prep Message Ingestion, 4-Tier Multi-Principal Scoping, Token-Budgeted compile_context, and External/OTel Trace Ingest
items.body:
## Spec IDs

`AI-05` · `AI-07` · `AI-08` · `AI-11` · `AI-12` · `INT-13` · `PERF-19`

## Context & Problem Statement

Issues `#2099` and `#2130`–`#2132` establish **Samyama Smriti**, our graph-native agent memory and self-optimizing teleprompter stack. However, when **external agents that are neither spawned nor controlled by `samyama-graph`** (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, or custom microservices) use `samyama-graph` as an external Agentic Memory Backend, two assumptions in `#2099` and `#2131` break down:

1. **Pre-Extraction Assumption in `#2099`:** `CALL agent.memory.remember(session_id, episode_payload, entities, relations, embedding)` assumes the caller already extracted `entities`, `relations`, and `embedding` vectors. External agents only have raw conversation turns (`[{role, content, tool_calls, timestamp}]`) and expect the memory server to extract entities/facts, resolve coreferences, and embed automatically.
2. **In-Process Execution Assumption in `#2131`:** `PlanExecutor` (`src/agent/executor.rs:148`) writes `(:Question)-[:USED_TOOL]->(:Tool)` telemetry edges only when `samyama-graph` itself executes the plan. When an external orchestrator runs tools outside `samyama-graph`, those tool trajectories and rewards never enter `GraphStore` unless an external trace ingestion surface is provided.

---

## Proposed Architecture & Deliverables

### 1. 4-Tier Hierarchical Memory Scoping (`MemoryScope`)
- Extend the `#2099` memory data model with a first-class `MemoryScope` envelope enforced at read/write time (`AI-12`):
  - `run_id` / `agent_id` (`visibility = "private"`): Scratchpad working memory isolated to a single external agent/subagent invocation.
  - `session_id` (`visibility = "session"`): Thread-level episodic memory shared across turns in a conversation.
  - `user_id` (`visibility = "user"`): Cross-session long-term user preferences, profile entities, and persistent facts.
  - `namespace` / `tenant_id` (`visibility = "shared"`): Organizational/team semantic and procedural memory shared across collaborating external agents.

### 2. Zero-Prep Raw Message Ingestion (`CALL agent.memory.ingest` & `POST /api/memory/messages`)
- Expose `CALL agent.memory.ingest(scope_map, messages_json, options_map) YIELD episode_id, extracted_entities, upserted_facts, superseded_facts`:
  - Accepts raw `messages: [{role, content, timestamp, tool_calls, metadata}]`.
  - Uses `SignatureRunner` (`#2130`) + Samyama's auto-embedding pipeline to extract entities and relational facts, resolve coreferences against existing `user_id`/`namespace` nodes, and delegate to `#2099` (`agent.memory.remember`) to update `[valid_from, valid_to)` temporal edges.
  - Supports both synchronous (`mode = "sync"`) and non-blocking background queue (`mode = "async"`) ingestion so external agent turn latency stays `< 15 ms`.

### 3. Single-Call Token-Budgeted Context Compiler (`CALL agent.memory.compile_context` & `POST /api/memory/context`)
- Expose `CALL agent.memory.compile_context(scope_map, query_text, token_budget) YIELD context_markdown, facts_used, procedural_rules_used, episodes_used, provenance_envelope, token_count`:
  - In a single `< 25 ms` call (analogous to `AI-05` `db.schema.forLLM(token_budget)`), retrieves and packs:
    1. Active temporal `:Fact`s for the `user_id` / `namespace` (`valid_to IS NULL`),
    2. Distilled `:ProceduralRule`s and past lessons matching the query intent (`#2132`),
    3. Recent unconsolidated `:Episode` turns for `session_id`,
  - Strictly bounded to `token_budget` with mandatory `AI-08` provenance node IDs.

### 4. External Trajectory & OpenTelemetry (`gen_ai.*`) Span Ingest (`CALL agent.memory.ingest_trace` & `POST /api/memory/traces`)
- Allow external agents or an OpenTelemetry collector (`INT-13`, `#1622`) to push external tool-call sequences, latencies, token usage, and outcome rewards/feedback (`thumbs_up`, verifier score, or task completion status) directly into `GraphStore` as `(:Question)-[:USED_TOOL]->(:Tool)` and `(:Episode)-[:LED_TO]->(:Decision)` subgraphs—enabling `#2131` (`GraphTeleprompter`) and `#2132` (`consolidate`) to optimize external agents identically to internal ones.

## Dependencies & Reuse
- Builds on `#2099` (`agent.memory.*`), `#2130` (`SignatureRunner`), `#2131` (`GraphTeleprompter`), and `#2132` (`consolidate`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `agent.memory.ingest`, `agent.memory.compile_context`, and `agent.memory.ingest_trace` exposed in Cypher, HTTP (`/api/memory/*`), and `samyama-mcp`.
- [ ] 4-tier `MemoryScope` isolation verified by integration tests (Agent A's `private` memory never leaks into Agent B's `compile_context`, while `shared` namespace facts are visible to both).
- [ ] External tool traces ingested via `/api/memory/traces` are selectable by `GraphTeleprompter::select_demos` (`#2131`) and compactable by `agent.memory.consolidate` (`#2132`).

labels.description: Findings from the scheduled Open Code Review (OCR) sweep

items.body:
OCR full sweep of `dev/v2.0.0` (PARTIAL) found 195 high/critical findings. Full JSON in the run artifact:
https://github.com/cbtw-apac/HarborRAG/actions/runs/41290730135
Some files were not reviewed; the marker was not advanced and they will be retried.

- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/confluence/normalization/macros.py:185-188`
  This strips query/fragment data only when the value contains `://`, but it leaves URL userinfo in `netloc` (for example, `https://user:password@example.com/path`) and returns scheme-relative URLs such as `//host/path?token=...` unchanged. Since these allowlisted parameter values are retained in normalized macro data, credentials or signed values can leak. Parse scheme-relative URLs too and remove userinfo as well as query and fragment before returning the value.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/confluence/query.py:98-98`
  Parenthesizing raw CQL does not make the appended space predicate an unconditional scope. A caller can supply `space = "other") or (space = "<configured>"`, producing `(space = "other") or (space = "<configured>") and space = "<configured>"`; because `and` binds more tightly than `or`, the first branch can return content from another space. Since this is explicitly the tenant-isolation boundary, raw CQL must be constrained with a parser/AST that combines the caller expression and configured-space filter at the top level, or the raw escape hatch must be disallowed when a space is configured.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/exceptions.py:100-100`
  `message` is appended verbatim, so a provider/HTTP error containing an authorization header, response body, or full request URL can leak secrets or sensitive content through this exception's string representation (which is commonly logged). Redact the message with the core security helpers or avoid including raw diagnostic text in the exception message; keep sensitive details only in appropriately protected metadata.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/document_transform.py:15-21`
  This contract permits implementations to return a `Document` with a different authoritative identity or `tenant_id`; the runtime bridge returns this result directly without checking those fields. A connector transform should be constrained to enrich content/connector-specific metadata while preserving the input document's identity and tenant, so connector payload data cannot rewrite canonical ownership.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/policies/http.py:140-141`
  A scheme-relative URL such as `//attacker.example/path` has no parsed scheme, so this returns it without checking its host. When joined to the configured base URL, it targets the attacker-controlled origin and can cause authenticated requests to leak credentials. Reject scheme-relative URLs (or resolve them against `base_url` and validate the resolved origin) before returning.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/connectors/sharepoint/allowlist.py:41-45`
  When `site_id` is configured, `resolve_site()` can synthesize `site` from config and `verify_site_access()` does not replace a configured `site_url` with Graph's actual URL. If the two configured values refer to different sites, an allowlist containing only the configured URL makes this check approve the site addressed by `site_id` without proving that its actual URL is allowlisted. Only match an observed/verified URL (and validate that `site_id` and `site_url` identify the same site when both are supplied).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/config.py:153-153`
  Setting this to `False` allows cacheable requests without tenant metadata; the cache controller then assigns every such request the shared `__unscoped__` tenant key. Identical requests from distinct tenant-scoped operations can therefore hit the same cached response, violating tenant isolation. Do not permit unscoped cache keys for multi-tenant use; require a trusted tenant identifier in the key or reject the request.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/security.py:12-20`
  The sensitive-key detector misses common credential names such as `private_key`/`privateKey` and camelCase `accessToken` (the latter lowercases to `accesstoken`, which is not caught by the suffix checks below). Those values therefore pass through `sanitize()` unchanged and can reach telemetry/configuration output. Normalize key separators and cover these forms (or use a more comprehensive sensitive-key policy).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/agent_runs.py:235-235`
  These data operations accept a caller-supplied `AgentRunIdentity` as the sole tenant authority; none accepts or validates a `StorageOperationContext`. Consequently the repository cannot verify that `identity.tenant_id` matches the authenticated operation's tenant, and a caller that can construct an identity can query another tenant's run (the same applies to `create` and `save_step`). Require the storage context on each operation and reject identities/checkpoints whose tenant differs from `context.tenant_id` before issuing SQL.
- **critical** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/alembic/versions/0008_authoritative_tenancy.py:78-80`
  If a source scope has tasks assigned to different tenants, `LIMIT 1` selects one without ordering or checking for a conflict. This can assign the scope and all of its documents to an arbitrary tenant, causing cross-tenant misattribution. Detect conflicting task tenants and fail the migration (or apply an explicitly defined safe resolution) instead of choosing one.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/alembic/versions/0013_control_plane_tenant_identity.py:35-36`
  This server default remains on the column after the migration, so every future insert that omits `tenant_id` is silently assigned to the DEFAULT tenant instead of failing. That can misroute tenant-owned control-plane records and undermine the storage-boundary requirement that operations carry explicit tenant identity. Use the default only to backfill existing rows, then remove it with `op.alter_column(..., server_default=None)` after adding the column.
- **critical** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/alembic/versions/0026_conversation_messages.py:118-120`
  On downgrade, this state machine cannot preserve non-alternating or tool-mediated message sequences: a second user overwrites the first pending user, the first assistant consumes the pending user, and tool messages are ignored. For example, `user → assistant(tool call) → tool → assistant(final)` restores only the user and tool-call assistant; the tool and final answer are discarded when `conversation_messages` is dropped. Preserve all message content or explicitly reject downgrade when the sequence cannot be represented by the legacy schema.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/conversation.py:217-231`
  These deletes bypass the owner scope used by the session delete. If stale/orphan dependent rows exist (possible on SQLite because this repository explicitly does not rely on FK enforcement), reusing a session_id for another owner lets deleting the new owner's session erase the old owner's messages, legacy history, and run state. Add tenant_id/user_id predicates where available, and scope the legacy delete by tenant_id as well as session_id.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/jobs.py:60-61`
  This write has no caller tenant context and never verifies that `job.tenant_id` belongs to the caller. A caller can therefore create a job for an arbitrary tenant, and can overwrite the state of an existing tenant's job by supplying its ID (the immutable-tenant check only prevents changing the stored tenant ID). Require the storage-operation context and reject tenant mismatches for both inserts and updates.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/jobs.py:85-86`
  This update scopes only by globally supplied `job_id`; it does not verify the caller's tenant. A caller who can invoke this repository with another tenant's job ID can append arbitrary events and advance that job's sequence. Require the storage-operation context and include its tenant in the atomic update predicate.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/memory.py:160-162`
  This storage boundary accepts the tenant solely from `memory.owner` and never compares it with an authenticated `StorageOperationContext`; a caller can therefore persist a record under an arbitrary tenant. The read/delete methods likewise accept caller-supplied `MemoryOwner` values rather than authenticated context, so tenant scoping here is not an authorization boundary. Require the operation context and reject tenant mismatches before any database operation.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/projects.py:30-31`
  A caller can pass `tenant_ids=None` and get an unrestricted project list; the same optional-filter pattern is used by project/source get, list, and delete. These repository operations must require and enforce the storage operation's tenant context, rather than treating a missing scope as a privileged unrestricted request; otherwise a missed/incorrect caller-side scope exposes or deletes other tenants' records.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/projects.py:71-72`
  This only compares the stored tenant with the tenant claimed by the submitted object; neither `update` nor `create` receives an authenticated storage context. A caller can therefore update a row in another tenant by supplying that row's tenant ID, or create a record under an arbitrary tenant. Require the operation context and reject objects whose `tenant_id` differs from `context.tenant_id` on both writes (and apply the same check to sources).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/usage.py:65-65`
  This write trusts `usage.tenant_id` directly and has no `StorageOperationContext` (or equivalent caller-owned tenant identity) against which to verify it. A record with another tenant ID can therefore be persisted under that tenant, violating the storage-boundary tenancy rule. Require context on this operation and reject a record whose tenant differs from `context.tenant_id` before persisting it.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/schemas.py:68-70`
  This FK checks only that the project ID exists; it does not ensure the source and project have the same `tenant_id`. `SqlSourceRepository.create` persists both values without checking ownership, so a source for tenant A can reference tenant B's project and be returned/processed as tenant A data. Enforce the relationship with a composite `(tenant_id, project_id)` FK (backed by a matching unique key) or equivalent storage-boundary validation.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/schemas.py:111-112`
  These job references are unconstrained and have no tenant-scoped relationship to their source/project. `SqlJobRepository.save` writes them verbatim, so a job owned by one tenant can point at another tenant's source or project (or nonexistent rows), breaking tenant isolation and job/source consistency. Add composite tenant-aware foreign keys (with matching unique keys) or validate the referenced rows in the same transaction before saving.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/publication.py:35-40`
  Both publication operations accept only document IDs and derive tenant ownership from the stored row; neither accepts a `StorageOperationContext` or verifies the caller's tenant. Consequently, a caller can publish or retire a document from another tenant if it can supply its ID, violating the storage-boundary tenant-isolation requirement. Require the operation context and reject a tenant mismatch before changing state (including in `retire_removed`).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/reindex.py:163-165`
  This repository operation accepts a caller-supplied tenant ID rather than `StorageOperationContext`; any caller able to invoke it can select another tenant's document IDs, and the storage boundary cannot validate the caller's principal/context. Require the operation context and derive the tenant scope from it for this query.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/document_versions.py:147-150`
  These repository operations accept only a version/document ID (and some query labels), not a `StorageOperationContext`, and their SQL lookups are not tenant-scoped. A caller that obtains another tenant's version ID can read or mutate its status/artifacts via `transition`, `mark_verified`, `get_version`, or replay, bypassing the required storage-boundary tenant/principal check. Require and validate the context against the owning document's tenant for every operation, rather than treating the ID or caller-supplied tenant label as authorization.
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/document_version_access.py:46-49`
  These ID-only reads have no tenant context or tenant predicate (`active_snapshot` and `get_version` have the same issue). A caller that supplies another tenant's document/version ID can retrieve its active-version metadata and artifact references. Require the operation's tenant context and constrain each query through `DOCUMENTS.tenant_id` (including the version lookups).
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/document_version_access.py:211-214`
  This repair-target query is global: `processing_fingerprint` is not tenant-scoped, and `anchor_document_id` only narrows by source scope. The caller passes a tenant-specific storage context when processing the returned IDs, so this can feed another tenant's document IDs and artifact references into that tenant's repair run. Accept/filter by tenant_id here (and propagate it from the caller).
- **critical**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/document_version_access.py:244-246`
  Replay locks and then updates the version and its cleanup job using only a caller-supplied version ID; this operation has no tenant context or ownership check. A cross-tenant ID can therefore restore another tenant's version and cancel its cleanup. Require tenant context and verify ownership through the parent document in the locked query before mutating either row.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/reliability.py:220-220`
  This and the other ID-only operations in this repository (including `cleanup_for_version`, the state setters, and `projection_manifest`) have no `StorageOperationContext` or tenant predicate. A caller that knows another tenant's version/job ID can read its manifest or claim/change its cleanup job; `record_failure` and `enqueue_cleanup` likewise accept ownership IDs without checking them against the stored document. Require tenant context and verify ownership at the SQL boundary for these operations.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/source_scans.py:93-95`
  These data-plane operations accept only caller-supplied scope/scan identifiers and do not receive `StorageOperationContext` or verify its tenant. Consequently, a caller that can supply another tenant's `source_scope_id` (or scan ID to `record_seen`, `complete`/`fail`/`cancel`, or `reconcile_removals`) can start or alter that tenant's scan; `source_item` also returns records without tenant filtering. Require context at this repository boundary and constrain every lookup/mutation to `context.tenant_id` (and principal where applicable).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/summary_cache.py:18-18`
  These cache operations trust a caller-supplied `tenant_id` and never bind it to a validated `StorageOperationContext`. A caller that supplies another tenant's ID can read or populate that tenant's cache, so this bypasses the required storage-boundary tenant enforcement. Require context on both `get_card` and `put_card`, derive the tenant from `context.tenant_id`, and reject any conflicting tenant input (or remove that input).
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/summary_authority.py:157-158`
  For a specific scope, this query trusts the supplied `source_scope_id` without verifying that its `SOURCE_SCOPES.tenant_id` matches `tenant_id`. A caller can therefore pass another tenant's scope ID and receive its missing document IDs (and parent IDs). Join or constrain through `SOURCE_SCOPES` with both tenant and scope ID for this branch, as the `@tenant` branch already does.
- **critical** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/ingestion_control/task_events.py:32-34`

  This adapter returns a core error but passes the provider exception into the shared normalizer, which stores it as `original_exception` on the returned core error. That lets provider SDK exception objects cross the adapter boundary and remain accessible to core callers (including their raw diagnostics); preserve only the sanitized core error details here instead.
- **high** other `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/rerank/invocation.py:51-51`
  This invocation returns LiteLLM's provider response unchanged (and `arerank` does the same), while both methods are typed as `Any`. That lets provider SDK response objects escape the adapter instead of returning the normalized core rerank schema. The direct calls also allow LiteLLM exceptions to escape unchanged, bypassing HarborError classification. Normalize the response and map provider exceptions here, or ensure this invocation remains strictly internal and that a guaranteed caller performs both translations before any adapter boundary is crossed.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/rerank/validation.py:121-122`
  This rejects only rerank-typed names, not the shared provider-reserved names such as `api_key`, `api_base`, and `extra_headers`. If one of those names is present in `allowed_extra_litellm_params`, caller-controlled `request.extra_params` passes this boundary and is subsequently merged over deployment parameters in `build_litellm_parameters`, allowing a request to replace credentials/endpoints or bypass request-header validation. Apply the provider-reserved set here as well (in addition to rerank-typed fields), so allowlisting cannot authorize overrides of protected parameters.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/budget.py:156-159`
  Settlement is not idempotent: the authorization ID is never recorded or checked, so retrying settlement for the same successful response adds its cost again. This can exhaust a spend window prematurely and makes settlement retries unsafe. Track settled authorization IDs (or otherwise make settlement deduplicated) before applying the cost.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/config.py:195-195`
  This setting is only attached to `ModelClientConfig`; nested models such as `TimeoutConfig`, `RedisConnectionConfig`, and provider-specific config models define their own `model_config` without `hide_input_in_errors=True`. When validation fails inside one of those nested models, Pydantic can include the offending input in the error (for example, an expanded credentialed URL), so this does not provide the nested-error redaction claimed above. Apply the setting to every nested config model or sanitize validation errors before exposing them.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/redis_config.py:43-46`
  This forwards the opt-in without any environment gate, so `RedisConnectionConfig(url="redis://remote/", allow_insecure_remote=True)` permits plaintext remote Redis even in production. The dev-only policy requires production to ignore this flag; enforce that at the construction boundary or ensure this model cannot be configured with the flag enabled outside development.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/secrets/aws.py:41-41`
  When no client or credential is injected, this resolver uses the cloud provider’s ambient credential discovery (AWS credential chain, `DefaultAzureCredential`, or Google ADC). The package policy prohibits ambient cloud credentials unless explicitly opted in; require explicit credential configuration or an opt-in before constructing the client.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/routing_state_redis.py:249-249`
  Each admission resets the entire sorted-set key TTL to the newest lease's duration. If a long lease is followed by a shorter one, Redis can delete the key while the long lease's score is still in the future, causing subsequent admissions to undercount active requests and exceed `max_parallel`. Keep the key alive through the latest member expiry (without shortening an existing TTL), or rely on score-based pruning instead of this TTL.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/routing_state_redis.py:226-227`
  `now` is supplied by each worker's local clock (and the read paths also use `_clock()`), but it is used to score and prune shared leases. A worker whose clock is ahead can prune another worker's still-valid lease and admit above the concurrency limit; clock skew can also make snapshots miscount leases. Use Redis server time consistently for lease scoring, pruning, and active-count reads.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/singleflight.py:227-230`
  The Redis lock is a fixed-duration lease and is not renewed while `producer()` runs. If production exceeds `_lock_ttl`, the key expires and another caller can acquire it and run the same operation concurrently; the token-checked release only protects the new owner's lock from deletion, not against duplicate production. Use lease renewal or another mechanism that prevents an expired lease from allowing a second active producer (and apply the same protection to `aexecute`).
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/models/runtime/telemetry_adapters.py:30-30`
  This serializes the complete event, including `input_payload` and `output_payload`, into application logs whenever the dispatcher privacy config enables input/output logging; `LangfuseTelemetry` likewise forwards those payloads to an external service. Model/document content can contain sensitive data, and the package policy forbids logging it. Exclude payloads from these sinks unconditionally (and keep telemetry limited to sanitized metadata/metrics).
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/parsers/common/models.py:131-131`
  `document_attempts` persists this caller-supplied text into canonical metadata without normalization or redaction. The PDF fallback currently builds `ParserAttempt.message` from raw exception strings, which may contain credentials, document diagnostics, or request-specific IDs/timestamps; that both leaks sensitive details and makes retries produce different canonical bytes. Persist only a stable, redacted classification/message here (and keep full diagnostics out of canonical document metadata).
- **high** other `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/parsers/pdf/engines/liteparse/engine.py:197-197`
  Including raw LiteParse results forwards provider-specific response data through `PDFParseResult.raw`, contrary to the adapter boundary. Remove this option or restrict diagnostics to a normalized, provider-independent representation.
- **high**  `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/parsers/pdf/models.py:21-21`
  This unrestricted `Any` payload lets provider SDK response objects or other unnormalized provider data escape through the parse-result model, contrary to the adapter boundary contract. Remove this field, or restrict it to an explicitly normalized/serializable representation so downstream code cannot receive provider types.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/cache/redis/scripts.py:10-11`
  `PEXPIRE` returns 0 when the key no longer exists (for example, if its TTL elapses before this command runs), but this script ignores that result and returns 1 anyway. The caller can therefore treat an expired lease as renewed and continue work without holding the lock. Return success only when `PEXPIRE` succeeds.
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/cache/redis/repository.py:51-53`
  This public property exposes the provider's unrestricted Redis client, so callers can issue arbitrary reads/writes without a `StorageOperationContext` or tenant-scoped repository methods. That bypasses the storage-boundary tenancy guarantee (and leaks a Redis SDK object through the repository API). Keep the raw client private to the implementation, or expose only tenant-safe operations.
- **high** bug `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/alembic/versions/0002_ingestion_stage.py:17-18`
  A database still stamped at the pre-consolidation `0001` will run this no-op and be stamped `0002`, even though it never ran the DDL formerly in this revision. Since Alembic does not rerun the edited `0001` baseline for existing databases, those installations will permanently miss the ingestion schema changes and later migrations/app operations can fail. Keep the DDL in this upgrade for databases coming from `0001` (or provide an explicit, safe version/schema-aware migration path).
- **high** security `packages/harborrag-adapters/src/harborrag_adapters/repositories/database/control_plane/alembic/versions/0009_conversation_memory.py:38-43`
  This foreign key only verifies that the session exists; it permits a memory row's tenant_id or principal_id to differ from the referenced session's owner. That leaves the database able to persist contradictory ownership, which can undermine tenant/principal-scoped reads or deletes

items.title: [Agent 2/8] Multi-Source Resource Library: Uploads, Telegram API & Authorized Website CLI
items.body:
## Mission
Deliver one reliable **resource acquisition and administration** system for documents from direct uploads, Telegram and authorized websites/terminal imports. The same `Resource` metadata, permissions, storage, deduplication and ingestion events must apply to every channel.

## Ownership / boundaries
- **Own:** `services/ingestion/**`, `apps/api/app/routes/resources.py`, `apps/api/app/routes/imports.py`, `tools/importer/**`, related unit/integration tests.
- Consume Agent 1's auth, storage, DB and job interfaces. **Do not** implement OCR/chunking (Agent 3), retrieval (Agent 4), or UI (Agent 8).

## Implementation guide
1. Upload endpoint(s): streamed multi-file PDF/DOCX/TXT/HTML/images (and approved spreadsheets), size/type caps, file signature validation, configurable quotas, SHA-256 dedup, immutable original, source/license/owner/page metadata and version tracking.
2. Secure storage: unique object keys; never trust user-supplied filenames; antivirus/scanning hook, quarantine status, deletion/retention policy, tenant-bound read/download URLs, audit of imports and errors.
3. **Telegram connector:** Bot API webhook or polling for files sent to a connected bot/channels where it has access, message/file IDs, original attribution, paginated list and retry/dedup. Support disconnect/revoke, secret webhook verification and rate limits. Historical/channel imports only via a separately consented, authorized mechanism consistent with Telegram permissions; **do not claim a bot can fetch arbitrary private chat history**.
4. **Terminal-compatible website importer** for the user's **owned or expressly authorized domains**: `somaloom-import web --url ... --max-pages ... --dry-run`, domain/path allowlist, robots/site policies, delays, crawl budget, resume checkpoint, canonical URL/dedup, HTML-to-readable text, PDF discovery/download, and provenance/URL capture. No login bypass, CAPTCHA evasion, scraping third-party protected sites, or unrestricted host/network access. Deny localhost/metadata/internal IPs (SSRF).
5. Source management APIs: list/search/filter resources; connect/configure import source; import preview/status/errors; re-import changed documents; cancel/retry jobs; manual metadata correction; deletion with audit.
6. Emit idempotent `resource.available`/version events to Agent 3, including stable tenant ID, resource ID, storage key, MIME, checksum, title, citation URL, license and permitted use.

## Proposed endpoints / event contract
- `POST /api/v1/resources/uploads` (multipart); `GET /api/v1/resources`; `GET /api/v1/resources/{id}`; `DELETE /api/v1/resources/{id}`.
- `POST /api/v1/imports/web`, `POST /api/v1/imports/telegram`, `GET /api/v1/imports/{id}`; `GET /api/v1/sources`.
- Output events must have `event_id`, `tenant_id`, `resource_id`, `version_id`, `source_type`, `object_key`, `sha256`, `license`, `original_url` (optional).

## Definition of done — final product
- [ ] Bulk uploads and library metadata CRUD work end to end with progress, errors, retry and deduplication.
- [ ] Telegram connector imports permitted new documents, remembers checkpoints, respects access and handles rate limits; privacy and historical-import limitations documented.
- [ ] Authorized website CLI imports scoped HTML/PDF resources with dry run, logs, resumability and provenance.
- [ ] All resources retain original copy, attribution, access rights and separate version identifiers.
- [ ] Invalid/malicious files, oversize content, SSRF attempts and cross-tenant access are rejected in automated tests.
- [ ] Import events reliably reach extraction and are idempotent; retention/deletion behaviors documented.

## 48-hour checkpoint
Working PDF upload + resource list + Telegram bot test import + one authorized website import command; basic retries, provenance and safety. Scale/historical imports remain open subtasks until final sign-off.

## Coordination
Agent 1 owns schema approvals and durable storage; Agent 3 consumes your ingestion event; Agent 8 builds library/import controls. Never place bot tokens or website credentials in issue comments, prompts, logs or commits.
